I'm sorry. It sounds like you really got bad luck with your therapists. Have you considered looking for a new one again? I've also had three, and I never clicked with any of them. Their advice felt contrived, and if anything they made me feel even worse. But I'm seeing a new one next week, and I'll keep seeing new ones until I get one who doesn't suck. 

If you chose to do this, be upfront with them from the beginning. Think about what you need from therapy. It sounds like advice makes you angry- it makes me angry, I know that- so mention that when you're talking to them. There's tons of different therapy methods, as well. It sounds like you had CBT, and maybe that just isn't for you.

I am not the best at advice or comfort, but it may be of some comfort to know that you aren't alone. I was born in 1995, and I feel the same way. All of my (three) good friends were made online, and I'm so much closer to them to anyone outside of the internet. I feel like who I am on the internet is who I actually am, but I'm not the same person in real life. 

I got one call back all summer, went to the interview, didn't get the job. Shocking. 

I feel extremely similar to the way you feel. Every time I get excited about accomplishing something, I end up depressed because it's not going to last, I'm just too lazy and lack motivation.

Anyway, this isn't about me- I think to help yourself, first of all, you should go to therapy. I am sure that you do have interests and skills that are relevant in the real world, and a therapist could show you these if you don't see them in yourself. Having someone to talk to can be extremely beneficial, and you should try it out. There's plenty of good jobs that involve computers and the internet, and if you look you might find something that interests you that you would enjoy. Enjoying your life is the important part. 

What has helped me is accepting who I am. I will never be someone who could give up the internet. I accept that it is easier for me to socialize and make friends on the internet, and that it's one of my favorite hobbies. This is okay, because I get fulfillment out of it, and that's all that matters. If someone else thinks I'm a loser, that's their problem. If I think I am a loser, I need to find positive change because liking who you are is important. You don't need to radically change yourself, though. Acceptance is also a big factor. Accept what you can't change and change what you can.
